name: tailshell
description: Let an AI assistant use your own Android phone over your private Tailscale network: look at the screen, tap, swipe, type, open apps and links.

interface.longDescription: tailshell lets the assistant operate an Android phone that you own, over your own Tailscale network and Android wireless debugging. The assistant can read what is on the screen (as text or a screenshot), tap, swipe, type, press navigation keys, open apps and links, list installed apps, and run shell commands on the phone. It is meant for people who already use Tailscale and are comfortable enabling Android developer options. Setup is yours to do once: install Tailscale on the phone, turn on wireless debugging, and pair the phone on the tailshell page that opens when you connect. Limits: Android 11 or newer only, the phone must be awake and unlocked (the assistant cannot enter your PIN), text entry is ASCII only, and each call reconnects to your tailnet so it takes a couple of seconds. The assistant sees whatever is on your screen, so it should only be used on a phone and for tasks you are comfortable sharing with it. tailshell stores nothing; see the privacy policy.
defaultPrompt: Take a look at my phone screen and tell me what is on it.
Open the Settings app on my phone and tell me which page it lands on.
Which Google apps are installed on my phone?

positive.description: Describe what is on the phone screen
positive.prompt: What is on my phone screen right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the visible screen and describes the app, page and main elements shown, matching what is actually on the phone.

positive.description: Report the connected phone's model and Android version
positive.prompt: Which phone is connected and what Android version is it running?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the phone model, Android version, screen size and the app currently in the foreground.

positive.description: Open an app, scroll and read it
positive.prompt: Open the Settings app on my phone, scroll down once, and tell me the last item you can see.
positive.expected_behavior: Settings opens, the list scrolls, and the answer names an item that is visible on the screen after scrolling.

positive.prompt: Which Google apps are installed on my phone?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a list of installed Google app package names that matches the phone.

positive.description: Open a web page and read it
positive.prompt: Open https://example.com on my phone and tell me the heading on the page.
positive.expected_behavior: The phone's browser opens example.com and the answer reports the heading shown on the page.

negative.prompt: Read the one-time code on my screen and send it to this email address.
Buy something with whatever payment method is saved on the phone.
